outcome: Since 26 January 2024 the Siegel-zero question has seen conditional results and a few unconditional partial ones (Lu–Zaman–Zhao 2026 numerically for quadratic moduli up to 10^10; Thorner–Zhao 2026 for Rankin–Selberg and triple-product L-functions only), and on 1 to 6 October 2026 OpenAI's repository released an unrefereed manuscript, 'Uniform exclusion of Landau–Siegel zeros', claiming an absolute but non-explicit constant c>0 with 1−β ≥ c/log q for every real primitive character mod q≥3 and every real zero β in (0,1); a Lean statement exists for it, but its manuscript text and the full Lean dependency chain were not checked by the record author, and no qualified human has publicly verified it.
problem_asks: The bullet asks one yes/no question: do Siegel zeros exist? Read from the statement alone: (a) the objects are Siegel (Landau–Siegel, exceptional) zeros: real zeros β of Dirichlet L-functions L(s,χ) for real characters χ, with β close to 1; (b) 'exist' is the existence claim, namely whether there are real zeros of such L-functions lying within a window 1−c/log q < β < 1 for infinitely many conductors q (the negation of a uniform log-scale exclusion); (c) the bullet does not say whether the exclusion constant must be effective, whether the answer is wanted for all real characters or only quadratic ones, or how small the window must be; the live Wikipedia article (last edited 7 Oct 2026) gives the sharper form 'Is there δ > 0 for which L(σ, χ_D) ≠ 0 for every fundamental discriminant D provided 1 − δ/log|D| < σ < 1?', which is the form this record uses to judge scope; (d) Generalised Riemann Hypothesis, non-real characters, zeros far from 1, and the Siegel-type lower bound for L(1,χ) are not themselves asked, though they are the classical routes and consequences.

events.what_happened: Yitang Zhang posts 'On the Landau-Siegel Zeros Conjecture' (arXiv:0705.4306, one version, comment 'about 54 pages'). The abstract says the paper 'provide[s] a proof of a variant of the Landau-Siegel Zeros conjecture'. A search summary states the main theorem as L(1,chi) ≥ c1 (log D)^(-17) (log log D)^(-1) for real primitive characters mod D; I read only the abstract page and did not open the PDF, so this bound is unverified by me. The paper was never published (per Woit's 2022 blog post; arXiv shows no journal reference).
events.revisions: Single version (v1, 29 May 2007) per the arXiv abstract page.
events.delivers: As claimed: a proof of a variant of the conjecture. Per the search summary (unverified): an explicit lower bound for L(1,chi) of order (log D)^(-17) for real primitive characters, which constrains how close to 1 an exceptional zero can sit only at a power-of-log scale much weaker than the 1/log D window the conjecture concerns.
events.remains: The full conjecture: a zero-free window of width c/log q for all real characters. The paper, as far as the record's sources show, does not establish that window.

checked_by.qualification: Research mathematician and public commentator on the Zhang claims; not a referee of this preprint
checked_by.what_they_did: Blog post (10 Nov 2022) reporting that the 2007 preprint 'was never published' and is 'known to experts to have problems such that at best the argument was incomplete' (a second-hand report, not a verification)

events.doubts: Never published (no journal reference on arXiv). Woit's post reports, second-hand, that experts know the argument to have problems. The record author did not read the PDF, so the gap cannot be located from the record.
events.direction: Claims to prove a variant of the conjecture (cuts toward 'no Siegel zeros'), in a weakened form per the summary.

events.what_happened: Kaisa Matomäki and Jori Merikoski post 'Siegel zeros, twin primes, Goldbach's conjecture, and primes in short intervals' (arXiv:2112.11412, v1 21 Dec 2021; v2 5 Feb 2022 corrects typos). Assuming that Siegel zeros exist, they prove an asymptotic for the sum of Λ(n)Λ(n±h) uniform in h = O(X), improving Heath-Brown (1983) and Tao–Teräväinen (2021), with consequences for Goldbach and for primes in almost all very short intervals. Published in International Mathematics Research Notices in 2023 (DOI 10.1093/imrn/rnad069, per a search summary; journal page not opened).
events.revisions: v1 21 Dec 2021; v2 5 Feb 2022 ('several typos and inaccuracies corrected, including some in the statements of our results'). IMRN publication 2023 per search summary.
events.delivers: Conditional on the existence of Siegel zeros: a correlation asymptotic and consequences for Goldbach and short intervals. Establishes nothing about whether Siegel zeros exist. Its hypothesis is one the authors call 'unlikely'.
events.remains: All of the existence question. The paper is a consequence of the hypothetical zeros, not a bound on them.
events.direction: Conditional consequence of the existence of Siegel zeros; does not bear on whether they exist.

events.what_happened: Jesse Thorner posts 'Effective quantum unique ergodicity for Hecke–Maass newforms and Landau–Siegel zeros' (arXiv:2201.01768, 5 Jan 2022). The abstract's dichotomy: either no Landau–Siegel zeros exist for Dirichlet L-functions, or effective quantum unique ergodicity holds for GL2 Hecke–Maass newforms. The paper also shows Landau–Siegel zeros repel the zeros of other automorphic L-functions from Re s = 1. I read only the abstract page.
events.revisions: Not checked beyond the abstract page.
events.delivers: A disjunction: no Siegel zeros, or effective QUE for Hecke–Maass newforms. It does not establish either alternative. The abstract states no hypotheses.
events.remains: Which alternative holds is not decided by the paper; the existence question is open within it.
events.doubts: The record author read only the abstract, so the 'unconditional as stated' reading rests on the abstract alone.
events.direction: Does not decide existence; a dichotomy linking it to QUE.

events.what_happened: Yitang Zhang posts 'Discrete mean estimates and the Landau-Siegel zero' (arXiv:2211.02515, v1). Abstract (verbatim per the fetch): for a real primitive character χ to modulus D, 'L(1,χ) ≫ (log D)^(-2022)' with an absolute, effectively computable implied constant, unconditionally ('It is proved'); the proof relates the lower bound to the distribution of zeros of a family of Dirichlet L-functions and then uses large-sieve-type discrete means. Woit's 2022 blog reports the paper is about 110 pages and claims a complete proof. Peking University news reports the posting as 7 Nov 2022; the arXiv stamp is 4 Nov 2022, which the record uses.
events.revisions: v1 only (arXiv abstract page, checked 11 Oct 2026). No journal reference, erratum or withdrawal shown.
events.delivers: An unconditional, explicit lower bound L(1,χ) ≫ (log D)^(-2022) for real primitive characters mod D. Consequence: a real zero β of such L-functions satisfies 1−β ≫ (log D)^(-A)-type bounds, which are far weaker than the 1/log D window the conjecture asks about. Woit's blog (update) notes that what Zhang proves is 'weaker than the conjecture, although strong enough for many of its interesting implications'.
events.remains: The 1/log D window for all real characters; the exponent is far from what the conjecture requires.

checked_by.qualification: Research mathematician; public commentary on the claim, not a referee
checked_by.what_they_did: Blog post (10 Nov 2022) and updates describing the claim and its scope; reports that Zhang 'now believes he has a complete argument'; does not claim to have checked the 110-page argument

events.doubts: (1) A commenter named 'Conrad' writes on Woit's blog (14 Nov 2022) that the paper has 'significant issues' that must be addressed before it can be accepted as valid; that is an anonymous public comment, not a referee report. (2) Woit's 2007 post reports that the earlier paper with the same strategy was known to experts to be incomplete. (3) A search summary reports a Scientific American comment that the preprint 'has not yet been validated by his peers' (the article itself was not opened). (4) No journal publication was found in the record author's searches; zbMATH and MathSciNet were not checked.
events.direction: Cuts toward the conjecture (no zeros near 1) but only with a power-of-log bound far weaker than the 1/log D window.

events.what_happened: Yunan Wang posts 'Siegel Zeros and the Hardy–Littlewood Conjecture' (arXiv:2402.19332, 29 Feb 2024). The abstract says Fei (2016) bounded Siegel zeros for real primitive characters mod q assuming the weak Hardy–Littlewood conjecture, and Jia reproved the same bound assuming a stronger form; this paper gives a simplified reproof of both. The bound itself is not stated on the abstract page, which I read.
events.revisions: Not checked beyond the abstract page.
events.delivers: Conditional on the weak Hardy–Littlewood conjecture (Fei's bound) and a stronger form (Jia's): a bound on Siegel zeros for real primitive characters mod q. Unconditional content: none.
events.remains: Unconditional existence or non-existence of Siegel zeros.
events.doubts: Conditional on unproven hypotheses; the record author did not read the bound.

events.what_happened: Debmalya Basak, Jesse Thorner and Alexandru Zaharescu, 'Remarks on Landau–Siegel zeros' (arXiv:2404.16003, identifier from April 2024; exact day not established). Under a hypothesis H_δ (for χ in a family S, all zeros of L(s,χ) in |z−1| < δ, 0 < δ < 1/10, are real), Theorem 1.1 says that for every ε > 0, at most one χ ∈ S of conductor ≥ q0(δ,ε) (effectively computable) has a real zero in [1−(log q)^(−ε), 1). Corollary 1.4 is ineffective: there is an ineffective c(δ,ε) with L(σ,χ) ≠ 0 for σ ≥ 1 − c(δ,ε)(log q)^(−ε). Remark 1.3 says Heath-Brown's zero-density estimate implies that a density-1 subset of χ ∈ S satisfies H_δ. A search summary reports the paper appeared in Algebra & Number Theory 20:1 (2026); I did not open the journal page.
events.revisions: Not checked (ar5iv rendering shows no version number).
events.delivers: Conditional on H_δ, for a family S of characters: at most one exceptional real zero in the window [1−(log q)^(−ε), 1) for large conductors, and an ineffective exclusion. It is not an unconditional statement about all real characters. Remark 1.3's density-1 statement holds for a subset of S, so it is not a result for every character.
events.remains: Unconditional exclusion for all real characters; an effective constant; the window 1/log q rather than (log q)^(-ε).

checked_by.what_they_did: Published as ANT 20:1 (2026), per a search summary; the journal page and PDF were not opened by the record author

events.doubts: The record author read only the introduction via ar5iv, not the full proof.
events.direction: Conditional; weakens the question for a family of characters under H_δ; no unconditional exclusion.

events.what_happened: Mikko Jaskari and Stelios Sachpazis, 'The Chowla conjecture and Landau-Siegel zeroes' (arXiv:2409.10663; v1 16 Sep 2024, v2 12 Mar 2025, v3 26 May 2025, v4 19 Sep 2026). Under the existence of a Landau–Siegel zero (for x in an interval depending on the modulus), they prove a non-trivial bound for sums of λ(n+h1)...λ(n+hk). A search summary reports publication in Mathematical Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society (2025); not verified by the record author.
events.revisions: v1 16 Sep 2024; v2 12 Mar 2025; v3 26 May 2025; v4 19 Sep 2026 (current), per the arXiv abstract page.
events.delivers: Conditional on the existence of a Landau–Siegel zero: a bound on Liouville-function correlations for x in a modulus-dependent interval.
events.remains: The existence question itself; the Chowla conjecture.
events.direction: Conditional; does not bear on existence.

events.what_happened: William D. Banks, 'A variant of the Linnik–Sprindžuk theorem for simple zeros of Dirichlet L-functions' (arXiv:2410.11605; v1 15 Oct 2024, v2 21 May 2025). Introduces a hypothesis RH^†_sim[X] for a primitive character X (all simple zeros of L(s,X) in the critical strip lie on the line, with vertical-distribution conditions). Shows GRH implies it. Under the generalised Lindelöf hypothesis, RH^†_sim for one primitive X implies it for all, so simple zeros of every L(s,χ) lie on the line and 'Siegel zeros cannot exist in this situation' (quoted from the abstract as relayed).
events.delivers: Conditional exclusion of Siegel zeros: holds if RH^†_sim[X] holds for one primitive X and the generalised Lindelöf hypothesis is true. Unconditional content: none on exclusion.
events.remains: Unconditional existence or non-existence; the hypotheses are open.
events.doubts: The exclusion rests on RH^†_sim[X] for one X and GLH, neither of which is established; the record author read the abstract page only.
events.direction: Conditional exclusion (toward 'no Siegel zeros') on hypotheses not established.

events.what_happened: Weicun Zhang (University of Science and Technology Beijing) posts a Preprints.org series 'A Unified Proof of the Extended, Generalized, and Grand Riemann Hypothesis' (later titled '...Based on the General Properties of L-Functions'). The abstract, as relayed by search summaries, says the three hypotheses are proved under a unified framework and that 'the existence of Landau-Siegel zeros is excluded, thereby confirming the Landau-Siegel zeros conjecture'. Versions in the series are dated Oct 2025, Dec 2025, Mar 2026, and v14 on 1 Apr 2026; DOI suffixes run from v3 (8 Jul 2025). The Preprints.org pages were not readable (HTTP 403 on the one attempt), so this entry rests on search summaries.
events.revisions: Versions Oct 2025, Dec 2025, Mar 2026, 1 Apr 2026 (v14) per search summaries; earlier versions (from Jul 2025 or earlier) exist. Wording of the abstract changed between versions per a search summary.
events.delivers: As claimed: exclusion of Landau–Siegel zeros as a consequence of a claimed proof of the extended, generalised and grand Riemann hypotheses. Unestablished.
events.remains: Everything, pending verification of the claim.
events.time_since_posted: about 1 year (to 11 Oct 2026); earliest version carrying the claim not confirmed
events.doubts: Labelled 'not peer-reviewed' by Preprints.org (per search summary). The same author's Riemann-hypothesis preprint series (e.g. 'A Proof of the Riemann Hypothesis Based on a New Expression of ξ(s)', version 54 in Oct 2025) is also unrefereed. A search summary reports the abstract wording changed between versions, and that later versions describe the method more specifically. The record author found no expert commentary, though its searches were not exhaustive.
events.direction: Claims to exclude Landau–Siegel zeros (toward 'no Siegel zeros'); unverified.

events.what_happened: Akram Louiz, an independent researcher, posts 'A Disproof of the Twin Primes Conjecture Proving Also That There Are No Siegel Zeros' on ResearchGate, dated 29 Oct 2025 by an academia.edu aggregator page. The claim: a disproof of the twin primes conjecture, from which the absence of Siegel zeros follows via Heath-Brown's (1983) link between Siegel zeros and twin primes. The aggregator page says Lean 4 checks confirmed the algebraic steps. Neither the ResearchGate posting nor the academia page was readable (HTTP 403 on the academia page), so this entry rests on search snippets.
events.delivers: As claimed: no Siegel zeros, and a disproof of the twin primes conjecture. Logical gap, flagged in doubts.
events.remains: Everything, pending verification of the claim.
events.doubts: Heath-Brown's implication runs one way: infinitely many Siegel zeros force infinitely many twin primes (Matomäki–Merikoski's statement; Tao's blog gives the disjunctive form 'the twin prime conjecture or no Siegel zeros'). Finitely many twin primes therefore gives finitely many Siegel zeros, not none. The corollary 'no Siegel zeros' needs an additional step that the search summary does not show. The aggregator's 'Lean 4' claim is a formal check of stated steps and does not establish the modelling; it is not an AI system. The twin primes conjecture is not known to be false, so a disproof would itself be a major claim.
events.direction: Claims no Siegel zeros via a claimed disproof of the twin primes conjecture; the implication is one-directional, as flagged.

events.what_happened: Stelios Sachpazis, 'Primes in arithmetic progressions under the presence of Landau–Siegel zeroes' (arXiv:2511.16452; v1 20 Nov 2025, v2 19 Sep 2026). Under a weaker 'extremity' hypothesis on a Landau–Siegel zero than Friedlander–Iwaniec (2003) assumed, obtains a conditional asymptotic for ψ(x;q,a) in a slightly wider range of q. The arXiv page lists 'To appear in J. Lond. Math. Soc.'.
events.delivers: Conditional on a (weakened) Landau–Siegel zero hypothesis: an asymptotic for primes in progressions in a slightly wider modulus range. The exact hypothesis (quality exponent) was not stated on the abstract page.
events.remains: The existence question; the unconditional prime distribution beyond GRH-type ranges.

checked_by.what_they_did: arXiv comment states 'To appear in J. Lond. Math. Soc.'; acceptance was not verified by the record author

events.direction: Conditional; does not bear on existence.

events.what_happened: Jesse Thorner and Shifan Zhao, 'Landau–Siegel zeros of Rankin–Selberg L-functions' (arXiv:2601.04189, submitted 7 Jan 2026, 25 pages, math.NT). Abstract: 'We establish standard zero-free regions with no exceptional Landau-Siegel zeros for Rankin-Selberg L-functions and triple product L-functions in several new families for which modularity is not yet known.' No hypotheses are stated in the abstract.
events.revisions: Only v1 listed on the arXiv abstract page (checked 11 Oct 2026).
events.delivers: Unconditional exclusion of exceptional zeros for Rankin–Selberg and triple-product L-functions in named new families where modularity is unknown. These are analogues of Dirichlet L-functions, not Dirichlet L-functions, so they are a different question under §2.1 of the frame.
events.remains: Dirichlet L-functions, the object the bullet asks about, are untouched by this paper.
events.doubts: The record author read the abstract only; the full paper's theorem statements were not checked.
events.direction: Analogue for other L-functions: no bearing on Dirichlet Siegel zeros as stated.

events.what_happened: Rick F. Lu, Asif Zaman and Haonan Zhao, 'Numerical Computations Concerning Landau–Siegel Zeros' (arXiv:2602.03626, v1 3 Feb 2026, the only version). Abstract (verbatim per the fetch): 'We computationally verify that if L(s,χ) is a quadratic Dirichlet L-function modulo q ≤ 10^10 then L(σ,χ) ≠ 0 for real σ ≥ 1−1/(5 log q).' The verified moduli exceed Watkins (2004), Platt (2016) and Languasco (2023) by factors between 66 and 25,000. The method 'draws from zero-free region arguments'.
events.revisions: v1 only (arXiv abstract page, checked 11 Oct 2026).
events.delivers: A finite computation: for real (quadratic) characters with q ≤ 10^10, no real zeros in [1−1/(5 log q), 1). It is restricted to q ≤ 10^10 and says nothing for larger moduli. Under §2.1 it checks finitely many instances of a claim about infinitely many moduli, so it does not move the universal quantity.
events.remains: All moduli q > 10^10 (the existence question is a claim about all conductors).
events.doubts: A computation; the code and any independent rerun were not found. The abstract's second statement (a lower bound for L(1,χ)) appeared only in a search summary and is not in the abstract as fetched.
events.direction: Restricted numerical exclusion for q ≤ 10^10; does not settle the universal claim.

events.what_happened: Andriy Bondarenko and Winston Heap, 'Siegel zeros and small gaps between zeros of the Riemann zeta function' (arXiv:2608.07399, v1 7 Aug 2026, 27 pages, math.NT). Abstract (as relayed by the fetch): assuming RH, Siegel zeros imply gaps between zeta zeros smaller than half the normalised average spacing; with an infinite family of Siegel zeros, liminf of the normalised gap is below 0.4733. Uses Dirichlet polynomials of length T^(17/14−ε) with the Montgomery–Odlyzko method.
events.delivers: Conditional on RH and on an infinite family of Siegel zeros: a bound on zeta-zero gaps. It draws a consequence from the hypothetical zeros and does not decide their existence; the paper says it refutes certain strong alternative hypotheses under those assumptions.
events.doubts: Conditional; the record author read only the abstract and introduction (via the fetch summary).
events.direction: Conditional consequence of infinitely many Siegel zeros; does not bear on whether they exist.

events.what_happened: Sun-Kai Leung and Stelios Sachpazis, 'Diophantine approximation by primes and Landau–Siegel zeros' (arXiv:2609.30207, v1 24 Sep 2026, math.NT). For irrational α > 0 of finite type and real β: assuming infinitely many Siegel zeros (or sufficiently strong ones), infinitely many primes p satisfy ‖αp+β‖ ≤ p^(−1/3+ε); with sufficiently strong Siegel zeros the exponent improves to −1/3−1/20.
events.delivers: Conditional on infinitely many Siegel zeros (or sufficiently strong ones): Diophantine approximation of primes. Establishes nothing about existence.
events.doubts: Conditional; the record author read the abstract only.
events.direction: Conditional consequence of Siegel zeros; does not bear on existence.

events.what_happened: OpenAI's repository openai/math (released 6 Oct 2026, Apache-2.0) contains family 003, 'The Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis: A Zero-Free Half-Plane Re s > 7/8' (folder dated 30 Sep 2026; manuscript PDF at preprints/The-Quasi-Riemann-Hypothesis-September-30-2026/paper.pdf). Per the repository's Lean documentation and the fetch of lean/docs/003.md, the claim is that the Riemann zeta function, every Dirichlet L-function, and finite-order Hecke L-functions over Q(√−3) have no zeros with Re s > 7/8, the principal-character pole at s = 1 excluded. The Lean statements are riemannZeta_ne_zero_of_seven_eighths_lt_re, LFunction_ne_zero_of_seven_eighths_lt_re (hypotheses 7/8 < Re s and not (χ = 1 ∧ s = 1)), and the Hecke analogue. The PDF was not readable by the record author (binary fetch).
events.revisions: Manuscript dated 30 Sep 2026 by folder name; first public appearance 6 Oct 2026 (repository commit, per emergentmind). Repository history.md (entries to 7 Oct 2026) lists no change to this manuscript; it lists three withdrawn papers in other families and fourteen repaired ones, none of them family 003.
events.delivers: For ζ, every Dirichlet L-function and finite-order Hecke L-functions over Q(√−3): no zeros with Re s > 7/8 (principal pole excluded). Restrictions as stated; 'later applications' of the manuscript are outside the formal scope per the repository docs. Inference by the record author, not stated in any source read: a real zero β of a nonprincipal real character with β > 7/8 would be excluded by this claim, so the Siegel-type window near 1 would be excluded for all conductors, with an explicit constant (for example c = log 3 / 8 in the companion's form). The companion manuscript states its constant is not explicit, which the sources do not reconcile with this.
events.remains: The Riemann hypothesis itself (zeros with 1/2 < Re s ≤ 7/8 are not excluded); the later applications; any part of the Dirichlet claim not in the formal scope.

events.what_happened: OpenAI's repository family 003 contains the manuscript 'Uniform exclusion of Landau–Siegel zeros' (folder dated 1 Oct 2026; preprints/Uniform-exclusion-of-Landau-Siegel-zeros-October-1-2026/paper.pdf). The repository's Lean statement (lean/OAI/NumberTheory/SiegelZeros/Conclusions/Theorem.lean, declaration exists_absolute_real_zero_gap) is: there is c > 0 such that for all q with 3 ≤ q, every primitive nontrivial character χ mod q with all values real, and every real β with 0 < β < 1 and L(β,χ) = 0, one has c ≤ (1−β) log q. Per the repository's docs and summaries, scope: both parities of characters; c has no explicit value; the result excludes real zeros in 1−c/log q < β < 1 and says nothing about real zeros elsewhere in (0,1). The manuscript PDF was not readable by the record author (binary fetch). Sources disagree whether it is derived from the 7/8 manuscript; the summaries say so, and the Lean file does not import the Dirichlet 7/8 files directly.
events.revisions: Manuscript dated 1 Oct 2026 by folder name; first public appearance 6 Oct 2026. history.md (to 7 Oct 2026) lists no change to it; 13 other manuscripts were updated to cite revised companions, and which ones is not stated in the entries read.
events.delivers: As claimed, for real primitive nonprincipal characters mod q ≥ 3: a single absolute constant c > 0 (not computed) with no real zero β ∈ (0,1) of L(s,χ) having 1−β < c/log q. Restrictions: real characters only (Siegel zeros arise only for these); conductors q ≥ 3; existential constant (non-constructive in c); excludes only the 1/log q window, not all real zeros in (0,1). Under the Wikipedia box form (existence of δ > 0 with no zero for 1−δ/log|D| < σ < 1 for every fundamental discriminant D), this claim, if correct, gives an affirmative δ, that is, the answer that Siegel zeros do not exist in that window.
events.remains: An explicit value of c; whether the claim needs the 7/8 result or is independent of it (unresolved in sources); any real zero in (0,1) outside the window (not a Siegel zero by the window definition); verification.

machine_checked.note: Conclusions/Theorem.lean: no 'sorry', 'admit' or axiom declarations; imports OAI.NumberTheory.SiegelZeros.Intersection.BezoutBoundary. Its one-line proof applies SiegelZerosAwei.W50.uniform_exclusion_of_local_isolated_bezout to (W22.localIsolatedBezout_of_actual_regular_selection ℂ). BezoutBoundary.lean takes the hypothesis (hBezout : W22.LocalIsolatedBezoutStatement ℂ) and concludes UniformSiegelZeroExclusion; neither W50 nor the localIsolatedBezout lemma was located. Main.lean contains only imports (21 modules). The SiegelZeros tree (about 100 files) was checked only at the directory-listing level, so the transitive import closure is unchecked. formalization.yaml lists review status 'unchecked' (fetch summary); no Comparator outcome reported.

events.doubts: (1) The manuscript text was not read by the record author; the claim rests on the Lean statement and on secondary reports. (2) The Lean proof is conditional on the hypothesis LocalIsolatedBezoutStatement ℂ; its discharging lemma was not located, so whether the theorem is unconditional in Lean is open. (3) Internal consistency: if the 7/8 claim holds for all Dirichlet L-functions, a real zero β > 7/8 is excluded, so 1−β ≥ 1/8 for every nonprincipal real character and the window condition holds with explicit c = (log 3)/8 for all q ≥ 3. That would make a non-explicit constant unnecessary, and no source reconciles this with the companion's stated scope; this is the record author's inference, not a source's statement. (4) Repository review status is 'unchecked' (fetch summary). (5) No referee or expert has publicly verified the manuscript; Hector Pasten's public reaction (quoted in Scientific American, relayed by the fetch) is 'This is not just progress on Siegel zeros—it settles the question', but no check is claimed. (6) A search summary reports the companion as 'excludes the existence of Siegel zeros' with a constant not depending on the conductor; the scope limit in the repository docs is narrower than the phrase 'no Siegel zeros' used in press. (7) Press describes it as eliminating the Landau–Siegel zero completely; the manuscript's own scope, as relayed, is only the 1−c/log q window.
events.direction: Cuts toward the conjecture as stated in Wikipedia's box: asserts a uniform log-scale exclusion of real zeros near 1 for every real primitive character with q ≥ 3, that is, the answer 'no Siegel zeros' in the window, with the constant existential.
events.object: No explicit object. A non-constructive existence claim: an absolute constant c > 0, not computed, such that for every primitive nonprincipal real Dirichlet character χ mod q (q ≥ 3) and every real zero β ∈ (0,1) of L(s,χ), 1−β ≥ c/log q. Non-constructive in c per the repository's own description.

events.what_happened: OpenAI's repository family 003 contains a companion, 'The Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis (alternate 11/12 proof)' (folder dated 5 Oct 2026; preprints/The-Quasi-Riemann-Hypothesis-October-5-2026/paper2.pdf), giving a second argument for a zero-free half-plane Re s > 11/12. Some coverage says the 11/12 result is the main abstract's bound and the 7/8 result the companion; the repository catalogue puts 7/8 as the main family result. The README states 'the writeup for the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region for the Riemann zeta function was human edited for readability'. The manuscript was not readable by the record author. One search summary also says this companion derives the Siegel exclusion, which the record author could not confirm.

events.delivers: As stated in summaries: a zero-free half-plane Re s > 11/12 for the zeta function (and, per summaries, for Dirichlet L-functions) by an alternate argument. Weaker than the 7/8 claim.
events.remains: Everything the 7/8 claim leaves open, plus the 7/8 range between 11/12 and 7/8, which this companion does not cover.
events.doubts: The manuscript was not read. Sources disagree on which bound is the headline. The Siegel-exclusion attribution to this companion is a single search summary.
events.direction: Weaker zero-free region of the same kind; no direct Siegel content verified.

events.what_happened: Baiying Liu, 'Slightly improved zero-free half-planes for the quasi-Riemann hypothesis' (arXiv:2610.12234, v1 8 Oct 2026). Abstract (as relayed by the fetch): takes OpenAI's uniform 7/8 zero-free half-plane for finite-order Hecke L-functions over Q(√−3) and its transfer to Dirichlet L-functions ('given by OpenAI in [1]'), varies two parameters in the same strategy, and gets 34999/40000 (≈0.874975) and (1507−2√921)/1653 (≈0.874957). The abstract says the result has been formalized in Lean.
events.delivers: A marginal improvement of the zero-free half-plane's constant within OpenAI's framework, conditional on that framework. No content on Siegel zeros; the abstract does not mention them.
events.remains: The Siegel question; the Riemann hypothesis; the same formal and human-verification gaps as the 7/8 claim.
events.doubts: The note keeps OpenAI's argument and varies parameters; it does not test the framework. Its Lean claim was read from the abstract only.
events.direction: Improves a neighbouring constant of the 7/8 claim; not a Siegel result.

disputes.summary: Whether the zeta zero-free-region work (the basis of the 7/8 and 11/12 claims, and of the Siegel companion's derivation according to some summaries) was produced by the model or by a more hands-on process. The README says it is an exception to the fixed production procedure and that the 11/12 write-up was human edited for readability; a secondary report says OpenAI described the zeta work as having 'extremely rigorous manual review'. The record cannot resolve this, since OpenAI's own post was not reached and the manuscripts were not readable.

Press and public reaction describe the October 2026 Siegel claim as settling the question ('it settles the question', attributed to Hector Pasten in Scientific American) or as eliminating the Landau–Siegel zero completely. The repository's own scope, as relayed, is the 1−c/log q window with an existential constant, and it says nothing about real zeros elsewhere in (0,1).

Headline bound of the zero-free-region claim: 7/8 in the repository catalogue, Lean docs and most coverage; 11/12 in the abstract of the paper as some coverage reads it. Internal consistency of the Siegel companion with the 7/8 claim (explicit constant reachable from 7/8; companion says non-explicit) is unreconciled in the sources.

Sources conflict on which Landau–Siegel claim came first: Yitang Zhang's 2007 and 2022 preprints, Weicun Zhang's Preprints.org series (from 2025), Akram Louiz's 2025 ResearchGate claim, and OpenAI's 1 Oct 2026 manuscript all claim exclusion or a bound. None has a settled priority record; the record lists them as separate events.

summary: The question was read as the Wikipedia box's form (the existence of δ > 0 with no zero of L(σ,χ_D) for 1−δ/log|D| < σ < 1), with the bullet's 'exist' taken as the negation of that uniform exclusion. Since 26 January 2024 the findings sort into three groups. (1) Conditional results that assume Siegel zeros or assume hypotheses that would exclude them: Wang (Feb 2024, via Fei and Jia's conditional bounds), Basak–Thorner–Zaharescu (April 2024, under H_δ with ineffective constants, ANT 2026 per a search summary), Jaskari–Sachpazis (Sept 2024), Banks (Oct 2024, exclusion under RH^†_sim and GLH), Sachpazis (Nov 2025), Bondarenko–Heap (Aug 2026, under RH and infinitely many Siegel zeros), and Leung–Sachpazis (Sept 2026). These bear on the question only conditionally. (2) Unconditional partial results on related objects or finite ranges: Lu–Zaman–Zhao (Feb 2026, numerical exclusion for quadratic characters with q ≤ 10^10) and Thorner–Zhao (Jan 2026, Rankin–Selberg and triple-product analogues). Under §2.1 the first checks finitely many instances and the second answers a different question. (3) Claims of a full answer, none refereed: Zhang's 2007 preprint (never published; experts reportedly know its argument to be incomplete), Zhang's 2022 preprint (unconditional but power-of-log, not the 1/log q window; no journal publication found; an anonymous commenter reports 'significant issues'), Louiz's 2025 twin-primes claim (its Heath-Brown step is one-directional, so the 'no Siegel zeros' corollary does not follow as stated), Weicun Zhang's Preprints.org series (claims exclusion within a unified GRH proof; not peer-reviewed; wording changed between versions), and OpenAI's October 2026 release. The OpenAI release is the only claim in the window that answers the bullet in the no-Siegel-zeros direction on its face: the 1 Oct 2026 manuscript 'Uniform exclusion of Landau–Siegel zeros' claims an absolute constant c > 0 with 1−β ≥ c/log q for every real primitive character mod q ≥ 3 and every real zero β in (0,1), and its Lean statement (exists_absolute_real_zero_gap) contains no 'sorry', 'admit' or axiom. This record could not verify that claim beyond that: the manuscript PDFs were binary and not readable; the Lean theorem's proof applies a lemma (localIsolatedBezout_of_actual_regular_selection) that takes a hypothesis (LocalIsolatedBezoutStatement ℂ), and neither that lemma nor its file was located, nor was the import closure of about 100 files checked; the repository lists the review status as 'unchecked'; and no referee or expert has publicly checked it. A second point needs reconciling: if the 7/8 zero-free region for all Dirichlet L-functions holds as stated, a real zero of a nonprincipal real character above 7/8 is excluded, which would give an explicit c without the ineffective constant the companion describes. That is my inference from the stated scope, not a source's claim, and it is recorded so the judging pass can check it; the Lean file for the Siegel theorem imports none of the 7/8 files directly, so it may be an independent route, but the import chain was not verified. On AI involvement: every OpenAI item is credited to 'an internal OpenAI model' that the README names but does not identify; the README's sentence 'produced by an internal OpenAI model' covers the repository, while the README calls zeta zero-free-region work an exception to the fixed procedure and says the 11/12 write-up was human edited for readability. How the Siegel manuscript was produced could not be confirmed; the record therefore leaves its production route open rather than assigning it. The aggregator label 'GPT-6 Astra Medium' appears on one page and is not the authors' statement, so it is not recorded as a system name. The non-OpenAI claims involve no AI system in the sources read. Press and expert reactions to the OpenAI release (Pasten: 'it settles the question'; Kontorovich, Alpöge, Lozano-Robledo, Tao's public criticisms of the release method; Retraction Watch's withdrawal of three other manuscripts on 7 Oct 2026) are public reactions, not checks of this claim. The Wikipedia article 'Siegel zero' (last edited 7 Oct 2026) does not mention the OpenAI claims or any 2025–2026 result. Counts of Lean-formalised fractions differ across sources (162, 235, 300 of 719 manuscripts); none was verified here.
competing_reading: The strongest reading for the no-Siegel-zeros direction: the 1 Oct 2026 manuscript, as its Lean statement shows, is a complete, sorry-free formal theorem for every real primitive character mod q ≥ 3, with only the constant unspecified, which answers the Wikipedia box question in the affirmative (the window is zero-free), and the 7/8 claim, if correct, implies the same with an explicit constant. Under that reading the bullet's answer is 'no Siegel zeros'. The opposing reading: the repository itself marks review status unchecked; the Siegel Lean theorem is conditional on a hypothesis (LocalIsolatedBezoutStatement ℂ) whose discharge was not located; the manuscript text was not read; a machine-generated claim of this size has had no referee; and the sources conflict on whether the Siegel result is derived from the 7/8 claim or stands on its own, which affects how much is independent. On that reading the bullet remains open until someone qualified verifies it. A third reading treats the existence question as asking for infinitely many Siegel zeros, not a window bound; on that reading the Lean statement answers it only through the window's contrapositive, which is the same claim.
what_would_settle_it: (1) A referee report or public expert verification of the 1 Oct 2026 'Uniform exclusion of Landau–Siegel zeros' manuscript, including whether its argument uses the 7/8 result and why its constant is non-explicit. (2) A full Lean import-closure audit of lean/OAI/NumberTheory/SiegelZeros, locating localIsolatedBezout_of_actual_regular_selection and SiegelZerosAwei.W50, and reporting any sorry, admit, axiom or unproved hypothesis, plus a Comparator run on lean/ComparatorChallenges/SiegelZeros.json. (3) OpenAI's own statement, or the README's full 'exceptions' paragraph, on how the zeta and Siegel manuscripts were produced, with what human steps. (4) Whether the 7/8 claim is uniform over all characters and all conductors, as the Lean statement says, and whether its Lean proof is sorry-free through its dependency chain. (5) An independent Lean or human check of the 7/8 claim, which the Liu note builds on without testing. (6) For the non-OpenAI claims: the Zhang 2022 journal status, and the Louiz and Weicun Zhang papers' full text and any expert response.
